groups.group: Italian civil registers, read in the original

rows.what: Stato civile napoleonico 1809-1815, restaurazione 1816-1865, italiano 1866-1943. 327 volumes listed here.
rows.usedFor: The Arena spine from Rocco back to FILIPPO ARENA and SANTA UNGARO in the 1720s; the Arlotta, the Costa, the Donato and the Polistena.

rows.what: Twenty-two volumes, 1810-1865. Each bundle holds the BIRTH EXTRACTS of both spouses and the DEATH ACTS of dead parents, copied out of the parish books.
rows.usedFor: Filippo Arena's baptism of 25 March 1793, Domenica Costa's of 16 June 1787, and Giovanni de Costa's death of 29 March 1790 -- the oldest dated event in this archive.
rows.note: The processetti sit in the same Scilla holding as the registers above; the portal filters them by tipologia once the place is open.

rows.what: 457 registers, 1820-1893, plus nine volumes of Riveli di anime e di terre from 1714 and 1747-1752.
rows.usedFor: The Mazza spine to MARIANO MAZZA and MARIA CATALANO, born about 1809; four more children for Rosario and Leonarda; and the absence of any Mazza in the town's 1747 household census.

rows.what: The Calabrian side. Briatico has 555 registers of which this archive has listed 80.
rows.usedFor: The Prostamo to 1697, the Ventrice, the Cichello and the Melluso -- and the 1849 marriage bundle that proved three generations at once.
rows.note: The link opens Briatico, the first of the four. Zambrone, Pizzo and Potenzoni are separate localita searches on the same portal.

rows.what: Some comuni have their acts indexed BY NAME with parents and spouse: Scilla deaths 1911-1943, Pizzo births 1868-1903, Catania deaths 1911 onward.
rows.usedFor: One query replaces a volume sweep where it exists. Five of the eight comuni this family touches are not indexed at all.

rows.what: Internee dossiers, aliens registration, naturalisation, immigration correspondence. The item TITLE carries the particulars even when nothing is digitised.
rows.usedFor: Three men interned in the Second World War; Maria Nicotra's arrival at Sydney on 20 April 1962; the ships behind five family crossings.

rows.source: Queensland Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages — historical index

rows.usedFor: Twenty-eight registrations, including the one that names John Nicotra and Venera Cassaneti -- and the sweep that showed «Cassaneti» appears exactly once in the whole index.

rows.what: The interment register, searchable by name, with plot numbers.
